title: Rebalance your week and protect focus time
background: Useful when meetings fragment your week and you want to review the tradeoffs before changing your calendar.
inputs: Your Outlook calendar, weekly priorities, and personal constraints.
output: Meeting-load summary, conflicts, and a prioritized calendar-change proposal.
prompt:
Help me organize my week. Review my Outlook calendar for [week]. Summarize total meetings and hours, existing focus blocks of two or more hours, and the days with the most meetings.

Before proposing changes, ask about my goals, manager and management chain, personal commitments, and how to prioritize conflicts. Consider relevance, attendee count, and whether my manager is attending.

Show proposed accepts, declines, reschedules, and focus blocks with explanations, highest-impact first. Protect existing focus blocks. Draft any messages to organizers. Show each proposed change separately for review; do not apply it yet.

title: Wrap up a project and organize its work
background: Use at project close to make deliverables findable without immediately moving or sharing files.
inputs: [Project name], related OneDrive files, and the intended internal audience.
output: Proposed archive structure and a linked HTML project recap.
prompt:
I just wrapped up [Project name]. Find related documents, decks, and spreadsheets in my OneDrive.

Propose an archive folder called '[Project name] - Archive' and list the files that belong there. Flag uncertain matches, duplicates, and existing sharing implications. Show the proposed moves and intended audience [team] for my approval before creating a shared archive or moving anything.

Draft a lightweight HTML recap with a one-paragraph 'what shipped' summary, project outcomes, key contributors, and links to the headline deliverables. Keep links pointed at their current locations until any move is approved.

title: Catch up on unanswered messages
background: Find direct questions you have not answered and distinguish acknowledgments from substantive responses.
inputs: This week's Outlook email and Teams conversations.
output: Prioritized response list and draft replies linked to their original threads.
prompt:
Go through my Teams messages and emails from [time period] where someone asked me a direct question and I have not responded.

Separate quick acknowledgments from questions that need a substantive answer. For each, link to the original thread, explain what is being asked, and draft an appropriate reply grounded in the conversation. Flag missing information or decisions I must supply.

Show me both the acknowledgments and substantive replies for approval. Do not send even a short acknowledgment automatically.

title: Draft a metrics-grounded weekly status
background: Bring priorities, key meetings, and business metrics into a review-ready weekly update.
inputs: Calendar, email, Teams updates, and [Fabric IQ metrics or report] tied to your priorities.
output: Weekly status email draft with sourced metrics and upcoming priorities.
prompt:
Draft my weekly email to [team] for [week]. Use recent emails and Teams conversations to identify our top priorities and projects, and my calendar to highlight the key meetings ahead, especially executive-level discussions.

Use Fabric IQ to pull [priority metrics or report] and show progress since last week. State the reporting period, source, and any missing or stale data.

Weave priorities, key meetings, metric changes, risks, and asks into a concise email in my voice. Show me the draft and the proposed repeatable steps. Do not send it, create a skill, or set a recurring schedule during this trial.

title: Turn inbox newsletters into an intelligence brief
background: For people with more newsletters than reading time who want a coherent brief and a deeper research companion.
inputs: Newsletters in your inbox, [company], [industry], and public primary sources.
output: Linked narrative brief plus a separately sourced research companion.
prompt:
Search my inbox for newsletters, digests, and industry publications from the past seven days. Exclude personal and consumer newsletters.

Write an article-style brief with four sections: [Company] internal newsletters, AI and technology news, world affairs, and [industry]. Use flowing narrative paragraphs and link to the source emails. End with a short throughline connecting the week's themes.

As a separate research companion, investigate the most relevant headline stories using accessible primary sources. Explain the substance, context, key evidence, and implications for my work. Keep internal newsletter information out of public web queries. Produce this once for review, not a recurring email.

title: Prepare an out-of-office handoff
background: Make work in flight and proposed coverage visible before you leave.
inputs: OOO dates, recent meetings/email/Teams, next week's calendar, and your internal team.
output: Handover tracker, coverage questions, and proposed calendar/auto-reply changes.
prompt:
I will be out of office for [duration] beginning [date]. Build a handover tracker covering ongoing projects and tasks that need progress while I am away.

Review this week's team meetings, relevant emails and Teams chats, next week's calendar, and related files. Include project, status, next steps, deadlines, actions, proposed internal coverage, and document links. Include small tasks as well as major asks; mark coverage as proposed until confirmed.

Draft an out-of-office reply and a separate list of non-critical meetings to decline or delegate, plus meetings I own that may need coverage or rescheduling. Show all proposed communications and calendar changes for review without applying them.

title: Analyze OneDrive and propose a cleanup
background: Get a useful inventory and cleanup plan before taking potentially disruptive file actions.
inputs: A bounded [OneDrive folder or scope] and your relevance criteria.
output: Interactive file overview and a proposed reorganization/cleanup list.
prompt:
Analyze [OneDrive folder or scope] and catalog the files you can access. Categorize by file type, age, relevance, customer or product where supported by the content. State the scope actually reviewed and any unreadable files.

Create an interactive HTML overview, no more than six scrolling screens, with an executive summary and a final recommendations section.

Propose a folder structure and a cleanup list. For files you recommend removing, show the proposed 'Delete_' filename and destination in a 'Delete' folder, but do not rename, move, or delete anything. Explain uncertain relevance and sharing implications. Present the plan for my review first.

title: Build an executive command center with business metrics
background: Combine work signals with live business measures when Fabric IQ is configured for your data.
inputs: Calendar, email, Teams, priorities, and [Fabric IQ metrics/report].
output: Interactive HTML dashboard with alerts, work views, and a sourced business-health strip.
prompt:
Create an interactive HTML Executive Command Center showing what needs my attention today and this week. Use my calendar, recent emails, Teams discussions, and [priority documents].

Include an urgent-action banner, one or two high-priority alerts, today's next priority, busiest day, and working days left. Use Fabric IQ to add [business metrics/report] with current values, trends, timestamps, and off-target flags.

Provide Meetings, Priorities, and Org Pulse views, plus a 30-day interaction map. Recommend 'Dial Up', 'Dial Down', or 'Re-engage' actions tied to specific workstreams and evidence, not judgments about individual performance. Link supporting sources and explain missing metrics. Keep this a private decision aid.

title: Research a document set with a citation map
background: Turn a research folder into a defensible brief and check its findings against business data.
inputs: [Source folder], [topic], and a relevant Fabric IQ dataset/report.
output: Structured research brief, three strongest insights, and claim-to-source citation map.
prompt:
Review the documents in [source folder] about [topic]. Read each accessible document in full and list any you could not read completely.

Produce a structured brief covering background, key findings, conflicts across sources, and the three strongest insights with rationale. Use Fabric IQ to compare findings with [business dataset/report], showing where the evidence aligns or diverges. Do not treat correlation as proof of causation.

Include a citation map linking each material claim to its document and page or section, plus the business-data source and reporting period where relevant. Flag missing context, stale evidence, and follow-up questions.

title: Audit files against a standard
background: Review a folder against a brand, naming, quality, or compliance standard without changing the source files.
inputs: [Folder] and the approved [standard or policy document].
output: Sortable Excel findings report with severity, impact, and recommended fixes.
prompt:
Audit the [file types] in [folder] against [approved standard, brand guide, compliance policy, or naming convention]. Read each accessible item and report incomplete coverage.

Classify findings as Critical, Major, or Minor. For each, identify the file and location, cite the relevant standard, describe the issue and impact, and recommend a specific fix.

Create a sortable Excel report with total items reviewed, findings by category, common issues, and the recommended remediation order. Distinguish confirmed deviations from items needing specialist review. Do not change any files; give me the action list.

title: Build a 30-60-90-day onboarding plan
background: Ground a new hire's plan in the actual role, team priorities, and stakeholder network.
inputs: [Role], [team], [start date], job description, team charter, stakeholders, and SharePoint links.
output: Word onboarding plan, HTML getting-started dashboard, and proposed check-in times.
prompt:
[Name / Role] joins [team] on [start date]. Use [reference folder] containing the job description, team charter, key stakeholders, and team SharePoint link.

Build a practical Word 30-60-90-day plan with learning goals, stakeholders to meet, role-specific weekly deliverables, and manager check-in cadence. Ground it in the role's responsibilities and team priorities.

Create an HTML getting-started dashboard with a three-phase progress tracker, people map, and first-week priorities. Review my calendar and propose twice-weekly check-ins across the first month. Show proposed attendees and times, but do not send invites until I approve.

title: Build a customer deck from approved pricing
background: Use an approved pricing image as a controlled input, with a review gate before building the full deck.
inputs: An approved pricing screenshot, [product], [meeting date], and permitted account files/email.
output: PowerPoint deck and a customer email draft; pricing slide reviewed first.
prompt:
I have a meeting on [date] and an attached screenshot of approved pricing for [product]. Create a customer presentation using those figures exactly, without rounding or paraphrasing numbers. Flag unclear figures rather than guessing.

Show me the pricing slide first and wait for my confirmation before building the full deck. Then include a cover with [company] and date, a context slide from relevant account emails/files where available, the approved pricing breakdown, and next steps with placeholders.

Draft a short email to [customer contact] with the presentation proposed as an attachment. Keep it a draft and identify anything I must verify before sharing.

title: Sweep customer email for action items
background: Prepare replies to customer action items before considering a recurring inbox workflow.
inputs: Previous week's unread external customer email and [account team members].
output: Thread-linked reply drafts and a private review summary.
prompt:
Review unread emails from external customers received in the previous week. Focus on messages with action items for me or [account team members].

For each, identify the required response, owner, and any deadline. Draft a reply in the context of the original thread, not an unrelated new email. Where supported, stage it in Outlook Drafts; otherwise show the draft with a link to the source thread.

Prepare an email summary and a Teams self-message reminding me what to review, but do not send either. Run this once so I can check the quality before separately deciding whether to save a skill or schedule a Monday run.

title: Stage a full customer meeting prep kit
background: Assemble a multi-artifact meeting kit using the deck's file-based route, without a live CRM connection.
inputs: [Customer], meeting date, brief template, approved usage/sales workbook, and account email/files.
output: Word brief, Excel trend overview, PowerPoint pitch, prep-time proposal, and email draft.
accessNote: File-based variant. Supply the customer data workbook; no Dynamics connection is used.
prompt:
Prepare me for [customer] on [meeting date]. Use relevant emails, calendar items, and files to complete the attached [customer brief template]. For account and usage figures, use only the [approved customer data workbook] I provide; do not connect to a CRM.

Build an Excel overview of usage and sales trends and an editable PowerPoint covering supported competitive differentiation, opportunities, and next steps. Separate public research from private account information and flag missing data.

Propose a 30-minute prep block with [prep attendee] tomorrow morning. Draft an account-team update addressed to [contacts] covering status, findings, and proposals. Hold the invite and email for review.

title: Counter a competitor launch with a customer pitch
background: Translate a competitor announcement into a sourced comparison and customer-specific value story.
inputs: [Product], [competitor product/announcement URL], approved product evidence, and customer context.
output: Excel comparison, Word value proposition, and editable PowerPoint pitch.
prompt:
I have a customer meeting on [date] and need a competitive pitch for [product] following [competitor product announcement / URL]. Use public primary sources and approved product/account files.

Create an Excel comparison across the dimensions relevant to [customer]. Cite evidence for each material comparison and label unknowns or unverified claims.

Build a direct, readable Word value proposition explaining [product]'s strengths, differences within our own portfolio, and fit for this customer's stated needs. Bring the supported findings into an editable PowerPoint pitch. Keep private account context out of public research queries and hold all artifacts for my review.

title: Review quarter-end Commit risk from a snapshot
background: Assess at-risk deals using the source deck's uploaded-snapshot option rather than live CRM data.
inputs: [CRM pipeline snapshot.xlsx], closing period, and related customer email, meetings, and files.
output: One-slide risk summary, follow-up drafts, and an Excel proposed-update file.
accessNote: Uploaded snapshot only. This does not read or update a live CRM.
prompt:
Review the opportunities I own that close in [quarter] and are marked Commit in the attached [CRM pipeline snapshot.xlsx]. Use this uploaded snapshot, not a live CRM connector.

Cross-check each against available customer emails, meetings, and shared documents. Flag stale snapshot data and distinguish confirmed facts from inferred risks.

Create a one-page PowerPoint risk summary with a specific reason and source per flagged deal. Draft a targeted follow-up email for each. Create an Excel proposed-update file with risk flags, follow-up owners, and due dates; mark unconfirmed assignments or dates clearly. Do not import the file or update any live records.

title: Pitch an upsell candidate from an account snapshot
background: Use an uploaded account list to prioritize expansion hypotheses and build a review-ready pitch.
inputs: [CRM account snapshot.xlsx], renewal/engagement evidence, approved value proof, and relevant public news.
output: Ranked shortlist, five-slide expansion pack, one-page account plan, and outreach draft.
accessNote: Uploaded snapshot only. No live CRM or fabricated ROI figures.
prompt:
Using the attached [CRM account snapshot.xlsx], identify the strongest upsell candidate for this week. Do not use a live CRM connection. Consider renewal timing, recent engagement, executive changes, relevant public news, and evidence from meetings.

Rank candidates with sourced reasons and label expansion likelihood as an assessment, not a fact. For the leading account, summarize current state, value evidenced, unmet needs, and decision makers.

Draft a five-slide Expansion Pack: value realized, gap, proposed add-on, value/ROI assumptions, and close plan. Add a one-page internal account plan with stakeholders, timeline, risks, and next actions, plus a warm executive outreach email. Do not invent value figures.

title: Launch onboarding from a new-customer email
background: Use a specific new-customer message as the starting point for a coordinated onboarding package.
inputs: [New-customer email link], [customer], SharePoint destination, and account-team contacts.
output: Proposed SharePoint workspace, Word/PowerPoint onboarding artifacts, Teams and welcome-email drafts.
prompt:
Use [new-customer email link or exact subject/date] as the source of truth for onboarding [customer]. Confirm the correct message before proceeding.

Research the customer's location, industry, and revenue using the email and accessible public sources. Cite evidence and flag missing figures. Propose a SharePoint folder named 'YYYY-MM-DD [customer]' in [approved location].

Draft executive-level Word and PowerPoint onboarding artifacts and show the proposed folder contents. Draft a Teams summary for [account team] with the intended folder link, and a welcome email to [customer contact]. Do not create shared folders, change access, post messages, or send the welcome until I approve the specific actions.

title: Design a role-based customer learning curriculum
background: Create a sourced progression from first use to advanced application for a defined audience.
inputs: [Product], [customer role], skill gaps, and champion/power-user program goals.
output: Markdown learning paths with resource tables and a suggested rollout order.
prompt:
Build a role-relevant [product] learning curriculum for [customer]. First ask about the user base, whether this supports a champion or enablement program, and the known skill gaps.

After I answer, design Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced paths using public, accessible official [product vendor] resources only. Do not use internal or tenant-specific content.

For each path, provide a sequenced Markdown table with title, source link, completion time (clearly labeled if estimated), short summary, audience, and prerequisites. Explain how [role/persona] could apply each skill in practice. Close with a recommended rollout order for [program]. Flag unavailable resources rather than inventing links.

title: Model an executive value story
background: Build a transparent, assumption-led business case rather than promise unverified savings.
inputs: Public customer strategy, [product], confirmed KPIs, population, costs, volume, and realization assumptions.
output: Five-to-seven-slide executive deck and an HTML value model with editable assumptions.
prompt:
Create a business value story for [customer] and [product], as a five-to-seven-slide PowerPoint and an interactive HTML executive brief. Ask for the website, industry, personas, priorities, confirmed KPIs, impacted population, hourly cost, task volume, realization factor, and investment assumptions one at a time.

Research up to three public strategic priorities, quoting and citing their sources. Propose nine relevant use cases across [three categories], label them as hypotheses, and prioritize by ease and impact. Map pain to outcome and supported product capability, with KPI definitions and validation questions.

Build an editable value model showing its formulas, annualized value, investment, ROI, and break-even only where inputs support the calculation. Do not supply an arbitrary default realization factor or present estimates as measured savings. Close with an alignment, pilot, and measurement recommendation for review.

title: Compile a marketing standup brief
background: Bring campaign decisions and performance into one brief before the team standup.
inputs: [Team channel], marketing email, standup invite, and Fabric IQ campaign metrics.
output: Word brief grouped by campaign with blockers, decisions, owners, and performance changes.
prompt:
Before [marketing standup], summarize where each active campaign stands. Review the past seven days in [team channel], marketing email threads containing decisions, and the standup invite.

Use Fabric IQ to pull [campaign performance report]: week-over-week movement, underperforming areas, and the strongest signals. Cite the report, reporting period, and data timestamp, and flag gaps.

Group the Word brief by campaign, with cross-cutting blockers at the top. Include progress, decisions, owner updates, performance changes, and questions needing a decision. Keep interpretations distinct from the underlying numbers.

title: Recap research and insights sessions
background: Combine a findings readout, messaging review, and implications discussion into an owner-ready recap.
inputs: [Research project] meeting transcripts, related Teams channel, and follow-up email.
output: Draft Teams recap with decisions, open issues, and proposed next-step owners.
prompt:
Pull together this week's [research project] debrief sessions: [findings readout], [messaging review], and [implications discussion].

Read their available meeting transcripts, related [team channel] discussions, and follow-up email. Explain what was decided, what remains open, and what needs an owner before next week.

Draft a concise recap for [team channel], grouped into decided, open, and pending items. Include named next steps and deadlines only where supported, marking proposed owners or dates as unconfirmed. Link the evidence and keep the post as a draft for review.

title: Kick off a campaign with prior learnings
background: Use earlier campaign performance to shape the brief before creating a workspace or sending a kickoff.
inputs: [Campaign], [launch date], intake brief, related email, Fabric IQ performance, and stakeholders.
output: Word working brief, proposed OneDrive workspace, and kickoff invitation draft.
prompt:
I am kicking off [campaign] launching on [date]. Use the attached intake brief and related email threads.

Pull prior campaign performance from [Fabric IQ report], including channel ROI, message resonance, and conversion patterns where available. Explain the sourced learnings that should shape this campaign.

Draft a Word working brief covering objectives, audience, messages, deliverables, proposed owners, and 'what worked / what to avoid'. Propose a OneDrive workspace called [campaign] and a kickoff invitation with [stakeholders] for [date]. Flag missing inputs and wait for approval before creating shared workspaces or sending invitations.

title: Create a partner and channel activation kit
background: Adapt approved launch content for partner and channel execution without drifting the story.
inputs: [Launch folder], [messaging document], prior partner communications, and reviewer roles.
output: Word partner assets, Excel social-copy pack, and review email drafts.
prompt:
[Product/campaign] is moving into partner and channel activation. Use the latest materials in [OneDrive folder], the approved [messaging document], and prior partner-facing communications for tone.

Draft a partner one-pager, co-marketing talking points, FAQ, and partner email template in Word. Create an Excel social-copy pack with three LinkedIn variants, two X variants, and creative guidance. These are drafts, not requests to connect to or publish on social platforms.

Keep claims grounded in approved positioning and flag unsupported statements. Draft separate review emails to [partner marketing owner] and [channel marketing owner], explaining what each should check.

title: Organize event week in a command center
background: Connect event moments, briefing artifacts, and performance context in one private working view.
inputs: [Event/date], OneDrive materials, calendar slots, Teams planning, customer history, and Fabric IQ event data.
output: HTML command center, PowerPoint dossier, Word speaker/customer briefs, social copy, and follow-up drafts.
prompt:
Prepare for [event] on [date] using [OneDrive event folder], event-tagged calendar items, [team channel] planning, and permitted email/meeting history for scheduled customers. Use Fabric IQ for [prior event/campaign performance report].

Build an HTML command center with one row per speaker slot, customer meeting, content release, or social moment: status, owner, time, artifact link, and sourced KPI where available. Label metrics as of their retrieval time; do not imply continuous refresh.

Create a PowerPoint event dossier, a Word prep brief for [speaker], customer one-pagers, [X] days of draft social copy, and follow-up drafts for the top three customer meetings. Link each artifact from the command center.

title: Prepare an analyst briefing and rehearsal
background: Align positioning, likely questions, and speaker preparation before an analyst discussion.
inputs: [Analyst firm/date], prior interactions, accessible published research, product folder, and approved messaging.
output: HTML briefing dashboard and a proposed rehearsal invitation.
prompt:
Prepare for my analyst briefing with [firm] on [date]. Review prior emails and meetings with the firm, their accessible recent research on [product area], the latest [product/launch folder], and approved [messaging document]. Do not bypass paywalls or assume access to restricted research.

Build an HTML briefing dashboard with positioning, our top three messages, anticipated questions and evidence-backed answers, notes for [speaker], and source links.

Propose a 60-minute rehearsal with [spokesperson] and [briefing owner] 48 hours before the briefing. Show the agenda, attendees, time, and intended dashboard attachment for approval before booking.

title: Assemble a launch kit across every audience
background: Build a coordinated launch package with performance-backed proof points and a proposed owner-routing plan.
inputs: Launch folder, kickoff, executive guidance, owner map, approved messaging, and Fabric IQ baselines.
output: Word assets, PowerPoint enablement, Excel social calendar and review-routing plan.
prompt:
[Product] launches on [date]. Use [launch folder], approved [messaging document], [kickoff meeting], relevant executive guidance, and [owner map]. Use Fabric IQ for [performance baselines/proof points], citing periods and sources. Treat inferred owners as proposals.

Draft a customer announcement, executive blog, partner one-pager, field talking points, and creator promotional pack in Word; a sales-enablement quick-start in PowerPoint; and a launch-week social calendar and owner-routing plan in Excel.

Keep claims and naming consistent across audiences. Propose an owner-organized [launch workspace] with review deadlines sequenced by launch beat. Show every destination and review request for approval before filing into shared locations or notifying owners.

title: Audit assets for messaging drift
background: Find off-message assets, propose exact fixes, and identify the people who should review them.
inputs: [Asset folder], approved messaging, brand guide, and relevant manager guidance in Teams.
output: Severity-ranked Excel audit, proposed replacement language, and owner-message drafts.
prompt:
Audit the accessible assets in [asset folder] against [approved messaging document] and [brand guide]. Review relevant recent Teams guidance from my manager and flag conflicts with the approved standards.

Classify findings as Critical (unsupported claims or wrong product naming), Major (drifted positioning or outdated value propositions), or Minor (tone/formatting). For each, cite the asset and standard, explain impact, and propose specific replacement language.

Propose an owner from document authorship or latest-editor metadata, clearly marking uncertainty. Build a sortable Excel report with coverage, severity totals, common patterns, owner/fix list, and remediation order. Draft linked Teams messages to owners. Do not edit assets or send messages.

title: Prepare a coordinated competitive response
background: Give PR, sales enablement, and field marketing a consistent, evidence-backed response to a competitor move.
inputs: [Competitor announcement URL], messaging, battlecards, Teams context, and Fabric IQ performance evidence.
output: Executive deck, internal memo, customer talking points, objection sheet, and communication drafts.
prompt:
[Competitor] announced [move] at [public URL]. Prepare a coordinated response for review by [deadline]. Read the announcement and accessible coverage, then use [messaging document], [battlecard folder], and prior discussions in [team channel].

Use Fabric IQ to retrieve [approved share/growth/customer momentum/win-rate evidence]. Cite the reporting period and flag unsupported comparisons.

Draft a five-to-seven-slide executive overview, a Word internal guidance memo, customer-facing talking points, sales objection-handling sheet, and a Teams update for [marketing channel]. Draft a review email to [PR owner], [sales enablement owner], and [field owner]. Separate internal-only material from customer-safe claims.

title: Run a customer-signal sweep
background: Turn customer conversations and compiled support feedback into the next messaging and campaign questions.
inputs: Customer-call folder, tagged sales feedback, Teams channels, support exports, and accessible market research.
output: Word signal brief, Teams summary draft, and owner-specific follow-up drafts.
prompt:
Run one customer-signal sweep for the past seven days. Review call recordings or notes in [customer calls folder], sales feedback emails tagged [tag], [sales channel] and [customer success channel] discussions, compiled support feedback in [support ticket folder], and accessible [industry] market research.

Identify the top three themes, emerging objections, message implications, recommended campaign/content adjustments, and proposed owner follow-ups. Cite representative evidence and distinguish frequency in the reviewed sample from population-wide claims.

Create a Word brief, a Teams summary draft for [marketing channel], and tailored follow-up drafts. Do not connect to a support platform, post, send, or schedule a recurring Friday run.

title: Debrief a launch and prioritize next steps
background: Combine launch results and reception into an executive readout and a proposed optimization plan.
inputs: [Product/date], post-launch period, Fabric IQ results, creative folder, and leadership/customer discussions.
output: Word executive summary, PowerPoint readout, and Excel optimization action plan.
prompt:
Debrief [product] launched on [date] across [X weeks] post-launch. Use Fabric IQ for campaign results, channel performance, KPI movement, and conversion patterns. Cross-check [campaign folder], [leadership channel], relevant customer email, and [marketing channel].

Explain the results, top three drivers, underperforming areas, and differences from plan. Separate observed changes from hypotheses about causes.

Create a Word executive summary, an eight-to-twelve-slide PowerPoint readout, and an Excel optimization action plan with proposed owners, evidence, priorities, and dates. Draft routing messages to [executive audience], [demand generation owner], [content owner], and [channel owner]. Hold all distribution for my approval.

title: Review market signals and planning implications
background: Turn material market changes into planning questions and a sourced intelligence brief.
inputs: [Business/market scope], public news/filings, permitted internal research, email, and Teams.
output: HTML intelligence brief, three proposed planning actions, Teams update and decision-invite drafts.
accessNote: The source names Microsoft's Capital Markets for Cowork skill. Check its availability; no external market-data connector is assumed.
prompt:
Review market and competitor developments affecting [business/market] during the last week. Use accessible public data, current news, competitor websites, analyst research, company or SEC filings, and relevant internal research, emails, and Teams discussions.

Identify material changes in pricing, products, demand, entrants, regulation, supply, or analyst outlook. For each, cite evidence, explain potential financial/operational impact, identify the assumption or decision affected, and recommend a response and timing.

Create an HTML brief organized into Market shifts, Competitor moves, Business implications, and Recommended actions. Compare with [previous brief] if available; otherwise state that no baseline was supplied. Recommend planning actions for the top three signals. Draft a Teams summary and, if needed, a 30-minute decision-review invitation. Do not schedule monitoring yet.

title: Investigate a support case with evidence
background: Form a testable root-cause hypothesis from supplied case materials rather than assume access to a service platform.
inputs: [Case report], logs/screenshots, escalation Teams channel, and an approved knowledge-base file or SharePoint link.
output: Evidence-backed analysis, diagnostic questions, Teams draft, and engineering-review invitation draft.
prompt:
Investigate [case report] using its support notes, customer communications, screenshots, errors, and diagnostic logs. Supplement it with relevant [escalations Teams channel] discussions and approved troubleshooting guidance in [knowledge-base file or SharePoint link].

Give the most likely root-cause hypothesis, supporting evidence, missing information, two or three checks needed to confirm it, and a potential solution with recommended next action. Distinguish hypothesis from confirmed diagnosis.

Draft a message for [engineering Teams channel] and a 30-minute review invitation with [engineering lead] next week. Include the case folder, analysis, questions, and proposed solution. Show all three outputs before anything is shared or scheduled.

title: Triage SLA risk from an open-case workbook
background: Prioritize a supplied case queue without requiring Dynamics or another ticketing-system connector.
inputs: [Open cases workbook], weekly update email, SLA rules, and recent contact history.
output: Time-stamped HTML triage dashboard and stakeholder-email draft.
prompt:
For this trial, use [weekly open-cases update email] and [open cases workbook] to identify cases at risk of missing SLA within [time period].

Use owner, customer, priority, status, age, last contact, next action, and SLA target. Confirm the relevant time zone and SLA/calendar rules; flag missing fields instead of inventing time-to-breach values.

Build an HTML dashboard with one card per case, ordered by urgency, showing status, blocker, time remaining as of the analysis, and recommended next action. Label it a snapshot, not a continuously live queue. Draft a stakeholder email identifying proposed owners and actions. Do not send it, close cases, or create an email-triggered automation.

title: Synthesize service feedback into improvements
background: Compare compiled tickets, surveys, and conversations to find evidence-backed service improvement priorities.
inputs: [Product/period], customer-feedback workbook, relevant email, and meeting transcripts.
output: Presentation, prioritized improvement table, and Teams update draft.
prompt:
Review customer feedback for [product] during [time period]. Use compiled support-ticket feedback and survey results in [customer feedback workbook], plus relevant emails and accessible meeting transcripts. Do not connect to a live support system.

Group recurring themes. For each, capture representative quotes or examples, frequency within the reviewed sample, affected product or journey stage, likely driver, and recommended improvement. Separate evidence from inferred drivers.

Create a concise presentation of the strongest themes and three to five priorities. Include an action table with improvement, proposed owner, timing, and supporting evidence. Draft a summary for [customer feedback Teams channel] and hold it for review.

title: Build a daily executive command center
background: Find decisions, quiet commitments, and preparation needs using Microsoft 365 work context alone.
inputs: Calendar, email, Teams/transcripts, and [priority folder].
output: HTML command center and printable one-page Word summary.
prompt:
Build an HTML Executive Command Center showing what needs my attention today and this week. Use my calendar, recent email, Teams conversations, accessible meeting transcripts, and [priority folder]. Focus on decisions, commitments, risks, and workstreams where my involvement could change the outcome.

Show one or two urgent items, today's top priority, busiest day, and remaining working days. Provide Meetings, Priorities, and Org Pulse views with preparation, conflicts, deadlines, blockers, and quiet commitments.

Label recommendations 'Lean in', 'Delegate', 'Re-engage', or 'Protect time'. Explain the evidence and one next action per item. Focus on workstreams, not evaluating individual people. Include expandable sections, status indicators with text labels, source links, and a printable one-page Word summary.

title: Prepare a board or leadership pre-read
background: Make changes, decision gaps, and leadership asks clear before distributing a pre-read.
inputs: [Meeting/date], materials folder, performance workbook, board template, and relevant executive updates.
output: Cited presentation, gap list, feedback-request draft, and review-invitation draft.
prompt:
Prepare for [board/leadership meeting] on [date], focused on [initiative]. Use [meeting materials folder], [performance workbook], relevant executive email and leadership meetings, and our existing board template.

Draft a concise pre-read presentation covering business performance changes, progress against prior priorities, initiative milestones/risks/dependencies, open questions, decisions needed, recommended direction, and outstanding actions with owners and dates.

Focus on what changed, why it matters, and where leadership input is required. Cite evidence and flag gaps or conflicts. Propose the save location, draft a feedback request to [leadership team], and draft a 30-minute review invite for [timeframe]. Do not share, book, or save this as a reusable skill during the trial.

title: Synthesize the week and prepare for the next
background: Find repeated decisions, blockers, and commitments across meetings rather than summarize every call.
inputs: [Time period], meeting transcripts, related Teams discussions, email, and files.
output: Concise week-in-review email draft with next-week priorities and response requests.
prompt:
Review my meetings from [time period] using accessible transcripts, related Teams conversations, emails, and files.

Identify major decisions, unresolved questions, recurring risks/blockers/dependencies, repeated themes, conflicting direction, and missing decisions. Cite representative meetings and messages rather than summarizing every meeting.

Draft a week-in-review email for [direct reports/team] covering decisions, themes, risks, commitments, next-week priorities, and areas needing leadership attention. Make requested responses and proposed owners explicit. Show me the draft before sending. Run once; discuss saving a 'Week in Review' skill and an agreed time zone/schedule only if I later ask.

title: Build a launch and channel activation kit
background: Adapt one approved launch story across customer, field, and partner audiences without a performance-data connector.
inputs: [Product/timing], launch folder, messaging guide, kickoff decisions, and executive guidance.
output: Six audience-adapted asset drafts, proposed workspace structure, and distribution-meeting draft.
prompt:
[Product] launches in [timeframe]. Build an activation kit for customer, field, and partner audiences using [launch folder], approved [messaging guide], [launch kickoff meeting], and relevant executive email/meeting guidance.

Draft an announcement blog, product value proposition, seller FAQ of no more than 20 questions, explainer video script, organic/paid LinkedIn copy, and web-page copy. Keep naming, claims, proof points, and narrative consistent; these are content drafts, not publishing requests.

Propose an audience-organized launch workspace in [workspace notebook/location]. If notebook creation is unavailable, report the limitation before changing destinations. Draft a 45-minute distribution meeting with [marketing team], including timing, owners, channels, decisions, and workspace link. Hold sharing, scheduling, and skill creation for separate approval.

title: Connect customer signals with campaign behavior
background: Use compiled feedback and a performance workbook to propose marketing actions without live analytics connectors.
inputs: [Feedback folder], survey/social-listening exports, email/transcripts, and [performance workbook].
output: PowerPoint activation brief with three to five priorities and a Teams update draft.
prompt:
Review customer signals for [product/business area] during [time period]. Use survey results, compiled social-listening reports and website feedback in [customer feedback folder], plus relevant emails and meeting transcripts. Use provided reports only; do not connect to social platforms.

Compare themes with [performance workbook]. For each, capture supporting quotes/examples, frequency in the reviewed sample, affected audience/product/journey stage, related campaign-performance evidence, and the marketing implication. Distinguish correlation from a supported explanation.

Create a concise PowerPoint activation brief with the strongest themes and three to five prioritized marketing actions. Draft an update for [marketing Teams channel] with evidence, proposed owners, and next steps for review.
